image_description: A side-profile view of a reddish-brown horse (sorrel/chestnut) standing in a grassy field. The horse has its head lowered towards the ground, possibly grazing or sniffing. It features a uniform chestnut coat with a slightly lighter mane and tail. The background includes trees, a fence, and a building structure under bright daylight.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible in profile. The shape is elongated and equine. Ears are visible and appear mobile/natural. Eyes are visible though partially shadowed by the angle.
The neck is bent downwards due to the pose, but the musculature and arch are consistent with an equine anatomy. No structural anomalies observed.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The horse displays a standard athletic equine build. Proportions between body depth and leg length appear natural for a riding horse type.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Uniform brownish-orange to light chestnut coat coloration with no black points.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coat is uniformly reddish-brown (chestnut/sorrel). There are no black points on the lower legs, mane, or tail, which distinguishes it from a bay.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Mane and tail same color as body or lighter (flaxen).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mane and tail are visible and match the body color, appearing slightly lighter/redder, consistent with the sorrel/chestnut description.
The torso appears robust and deep-chested. The topline (back) is straight and strong, showing no sagging or structural collapse.
The tail is visible at the rear, hanging down with long hair strands. It appears natural and attached correctly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long slender legs with single hoof per foot.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All four legs are visible. They are slender and proportionate. Hooves are visible at the bottom, appearing as single solid structures without extra digits or fusion artifacts.
